# Thoughts on the plane: A Love letter to Jigra.

Jigra has soul. And soul supersedes everything in a film. 

When i spoke to Ishaan, he pointed out how Mutthu death had no impact in the film. Mainly since his death was given a very short screentime. And Satya's reaction on his death was also very short.

Contrast that with Bhatia Saab's death. "Tiger hu mai"  
Bhatia Saab goes out with a bang. And it's an emotional moment. And on few fronts.

A son loses his father.   
Satya loses an \_almost\_ father figure. 

Apart from these 2 individual markers, it's also how Bala sends him off. Bala hints him being shot, 1 information piece at a time. 

The volume increases. Satya gives callback to his fire playlist (something she earlier didn't care for)   
"Bhatia Saab, kya playlist hai\!"

We see his hand increase the volume of the song. But the music for us (the audience) decreases. Stillness is what we are cruising towards. 

Bullet hole in the windshield.

His hand moves towards the gear. We see blood. Bhatia Saab is quieter than usual.

Realisation slowly arrives the destination. Satya moves to the front seat. 

 \_Sad moment. Get together. Goodbye.\_ 

"Ab Tiger banna hai."

Light illuminates his eyes and goes out with a bang.

 \_Release\_ .

What a badass. Bhatia Saab got a well deserved send off. 

But what about Mutthu. Why was his death so short lived?

The truth is, it really wasn't.

Jigra plays a lot with callbacks. Muthu and Satya's fight was a callback to their previous fight. Where winning for Satya was a "good thing"

This time, the frame is different. Winning for Satya means dying for Muthu.

Satya isn't right. She's willing to let loose 6000 criminals back into the society. (Perhaps an interpretation of 1 innocent convicted is worse than 1000 bad guys free)

Muthu's death didn't need a long sendoff like Bhatia Saab because the fight itself was the point of it. The fight itself was the long sendoff.  
Muthu's death merely was the release for the... moment.

It was the moment where Satya's chance to do things the right way died with Muthu.

We can't turn back now. We are the bad guys now, \_par bhai ke paas waqt bahut hi kam hai.\_

Jigra as a film is full of thoughtful moments like this. Moments that might not sooth a writer itch to craft a perfect story. 

Because Bala is all about characters and moments. Sometimes the moments belong to the characters, sometimes they belong to him.

…….  
[**Threek\#1: Reverse Chekhov's gun rule**](https://threek.substack.com/p/threek1-reverse-chekhovs-gun-rule)  
You want to write for your audience. Without losing their attention. How?  
[Prashil](https://substack.com/@threek)  
Sep 24, 2023  
---

## **Think of movies as a playground.**

It’s a playground where your characters are **unfamiliar** to the audience.

And the problem with unfamiliarity is that people tend to lose interest (and attention.)

As a writer, you need to be in control of scenes that need higher attention or interest.

A way to go about it would be following the framework: **familiar \+ novel**

I call it **Reverse Chekhov's gun rule aka The Naked Scene Rule**

This is how you would write scenes in a movie:

![][image1]

Let's say we have a movie with **5 characters \- A B C D E**

and **5 Scenes 1 2 3 4 5** (**A** with a major scene in 1, **B** in 2 **C** in 3 and so on)

and their introduction is supposed to be in that sequence.

As a writer, you need to make sure you **don't introduce B in scene 2** as this would cause a loss of context and then a lack of attention and possibly interest.

Here, no one knows who your character is. There isn't any form of rapport built with your audience. He's a guy who’s suddenly entering your room (your playground) guns blazing.

“*Who the heck is this guy”.*

*“I sure as heck don't know him”*

**This isn't an absolute law** but if you plot the audience’s attention on a graph, you surely see a dip.

.

## **So what you do is:**

Let's assume B has a **major role in scene 2**.

1. So if B has a role in scene 2, Y**ou introduce him in scene 1\.**  
2. B will not need to have a major role in scene 1 as it's the room where A is supposed to go guns ablaze. B is just there.  
3. Now people have seen him —even if he has a small role of passing the gun to A.  
   People now recognise B. So when you finally start scene 2 for B, B isn't a stranger. We know him. He’s the guy who passed the gun to A  
   These minor mentions can be called **context bombs. (because your planting them in your scenes, like a bomb)**  
   ...  
   This chain can be maintained and C is introduced in Scene 2 maybe just a minor role. this way he isn't a stranger either in scene 3\.  
   Again **this isn't an absolute rule** but the idea is about not disorienting the audience/losing attention. maybe you aren't introducing a new character. rather you're introducing a new element. a new Planet, a doomsday device, anything. Any important plot point when introduced needs to be something or someone familiar.  
   .  
   What's interesting is how Marvel has an interesting leeway for this rule. it can introduce a new character in a completely **naked scene (we are calling it a naked scene because it’s a scene without the cloth of the context bomb)**  
   They can do so because if they introduce Thanos in a post-credit scene for the first time, they are still not alienating their audience because the audience knows Thanos from the comic books.  
   So basically this rule that we just came up with can be used as long the character is known outside the movie's realm.

### ***Bottom line: The rule is "show them before you really show them"***

***![22 Fun Facts About Kittens][image2]***

Here’s a smol cat for your *awwwing* pleasure.

**PS. Also, the sequence isn't important i.e. it's not important that B is softly introduced in scene 1 so his scene needs to be in scene 2 only. it could be in a later part too maybe like scene 7\. What's important is to make sure B isn't a stranger.**

PPS. Chekhov's gun: If there's a gun used in a scene it must go off before the movie ends. every element in the movie needs to serve a purpose.

# [ThreeK\#2: Voiceless characters: The Silent Companion to your story](https://threek.substack.com/p/threek2-voiceless-characters-the)

Is your hero likeable? how do you even make him likeable?  
[Prashil](https://substack.com/@threek)  
Sep 28, 2023  
---

If you want to build excellent heroes, you need to first accept that we are extremely primal beings.

We have a moral code of our own that trumps any legal one.

We are also built to like small cute things. but most of all-

## **We pity Voiceless characters..**

Who are Voiceless characters you ask?

In the context of a story or a movie they are \- Animals, moving inanimate objects, robots, fish.

### **for example \-**

‘Thing’ from Wednesday, Pikachu from Pokemon, Mooncake from Final Space, Groot from Guardians of the Galaxy, that ball thingy friend from Castaway, etc. (I haven’t seen castaway yet🥲)

![What Tom Hank's volleyball Wilson looks like now as Castaway turns 15 years  old | Metro News][image3]

**These “helpless” characters** gain the most amount of compassion from the viewers. Even though in some cases they might not be weak in a traditional sense. (Pikachu, Thing or Mooncake)

Having the **main character interact** with (or own) these voiceless characters (VC in short) can build/showcase their inner-self to the audience. And it also makes them more **personable and likeable.**

(Eg. The Mandalorian and Baby Yoda)

This may seem pretty similar to an existing writing device called “Save the Cat”.

## **But the main difference is-**

Save the Cat talks about doing something heroic to define the protagonist as a hero. Whereas the ‘**voiceless character’** idea is about having our protagonist or even any character interact with an actual voiceless character.

You can showcase **if we should root for the character** if he’s nice to the voiceless character (VC).

Or if the VC likes them back even though the protagonist might have a rough exterior. (A rude dude, with potentially a golden heart)

**A dog** can like a character who seems Evil or unlikeable (could be a monster). But if the dog likes him so do we. Cuz we trust the voiceless characters’ decisions more than the monster’s looks.

## **The Flip side of having a VC**

Maybe you have a character that hates the VC. And also he wants to kill the VC.

Then that character is most likely designed to be **disliked by the audience.**

..

Maybe the VC is just part of an encounter where **Character A** hits a VC. And **Character B** is sad because of this.

The instant a character hits a VC, We as an Audience have our perceptions made for 2 characters

* **One,** of **Character A,** who hit the VC \- we hate them.  
* **And Two, Character B,** who’s crying for the VC \- we sympathize with them and hence like them

![The Mandalorian Chapter 13 – The Jedi: Baby Yoda's real name revealed in  another exceptional episode | Web-series News - The Indian Express][image4]

## VCs also build your villains.

**You can have your Hero kill a baby** (a VC in this case) in a flashback scene, showcasing his dark past.

(The reason behind his action: Maybe he was a soldier,// or an assassin doing his job// or even a reformed mercenary. he’s just someone with a dark past.)

But in the present, **The Mother takes the role of a Villain** as she becomes a merciless killer hunting the hero and everyone close to him.

**The Mother** was the victim earlier. But now she’s the villain of the story

..

VC gave depth to the villain's story and a **legitimate motivation** for her being the villain.

## **Another way to use this-**

We can even show a fallen hero **without making us hate** him.

**Example:** Your protagonist could harm the VC. But we as the audience don't hate them but rather, we are conflicted. because of the time we spent with them as a good character.

**Eg.** when Eren from Attack on Titan killed a bunch of children from Marley, He became a fallen hero. We don't hate him necessarily even though he did hurt the VC. But we don't love him the same way we did anymore. He’s now a character that is still the protagonist but due to how he acted with the VCs, we feel hurt by his actions.

And we as an Audience are just disappointed and conflicted. Adding more depth to Eren’s character.

![Cool cat facts - Times of India][image5]

# [Threek\#4 \- Ned Stark Dies and We Gasp \- Notes on Character Deaths and Life](https://threek.substack.com/p/ned-stark-dies-and-we-gasp-notes)

Why are some deaths more deaths than others? Why Did Ned Stark’s death hit us as hard as it did?  
[Prashil](https://substack.com/@threek)  
Dec 13, 2023  
---

## **Why are some deaths more death than others?**

Why Did Ned Stark's death hit us as hard as it did?

What about Oberyn Martell (The Viper)? or Bablu Bhaiya from Mirzapur? or DiCaprio from The Departed?

What's the common thread that connects these character deaths?

![][image6]

## **Is it because they were important characters?**

Sure yes that helps but think about the feeling you get when the above-mentioned character dies.

Is it the same feeling you get when Arnold’s Character died in Terminator 2? or maybe the same as when Oogway passed on in Kung Fu Panda?

No, right?

Most people will say it’s the unexpected nature of these deaths that makes it so impactful.

But I’d argue it’s because of the **unfulfilled potential** of these characters that makes their death hard-hitting.

## **The unfulfilled potential of dead characters.**

All the characters mentioned above (from Ned Stark to DiCaprio) were characters who had way more to contribute to the story.

They seemed like they had an entire book written about their adventure but the writer decided to rip out the pages in the middle of the journey— and right before things got interesting in their journey.

**It’s like pulling the life support on a healthy athlete who was never sick to begin with.**

* **Ned Stark** \- Was potentially going to save Westeros. Was Loved by everyone in the city  
* **Oberyn Martell** (The Viper)- Was Gonna Save Tyrion and be his cool best friend and be that Dynamic duo like Bronn and Tyrion were. ( He was also very skilled to the point he bested The mountain.)  
* **Bablu Bhaiya** \- Dynamic Duo with Guddu Bhaiya. He was the Brains. Had a Blooming romance with Golu that was left unfulfilled.  
* **DiCaprio from Departed (Billy Costigan)** \- He was winning the game. His resolution was only pending.  
* **Shaalu Gupta (Masaan)** \- Was gonna marry Deepak. And give him that push to finally leave the Ghats and propel his journey forward towards a better life.

## **This is probably because of a human ~~flaw~~ trait—Regret.**

You’ve already heard the adage “Nothing is more painful than regret”

This is probably why the characters which leave a hole in your heart are characters that have the most potential and were left unfulfilled.

.

So *don’t just* kill off your characters “unexpectedly” to expect a crazy reaction. Subverting the expectation was never the secret sauce to these.

## **Possible Ideas to Explore:**

* **Promised land** \- **Map out the full potential journey** of the character. Without giving a glimpse of the promised land— deaths don't have meaning.  
  * You need to show the ‘Promised Land’. The promised land is the life and the world of the character if they hadn't died.  
  * “What would his story look like if he was not unalived” Essentially don’t just write the character to kill it off eventually. **Write so they can live**.  
  * “Write like they will live forever. but interrupt that journey midway.”  
* **The Death should propel the story forward** \- Meaningless death provides nothing to the story. Their death could be the reason other characters start their journey. OR Their death should impact the world as we know it.  
* **Relations** \- A character that has no relationship with anyone or anything won’t evoke any emotions. Make them have some real connection with anyone or anything.  
* **Make them rich:** If they are bland, they are better off never existing than being killed off to fulfil the writer’s fantasy. As they will not create any impact whatsoever.  
  * ”*If they never lived well, how will they die well?”*  
  * **Make** **people invested** in the character’s potential story.

![][image7]

* **Exercise in extreme restraint:** Despite the ideas mentioned above. if this is used more than it should be, it will hurt movies on a macro level.  
  * You don’t want to be responsible for the audience having trust issues over every good character just dying off.  
  * Don’t Hurt the Entire Landscape. This Cannot be overstated.

## **Bottom Line:**

When you kill a character, make sure **it hurts *you* as a writer**. Only then you can make your audience feel the same.

Think: *“Oh I had such grand plans for this character, but alas…”*

# Day 4 \- Thoughts on Eternals

So I saw Eternals yesterday and I'm not really surprised that I really liked the film overall. the movie has been getting a lot of negative and mixed reception but I withheld my judgements for after I would watch it myself.

I think many people were really curious how Chloe Zhao would pull off a mainstream and high-scale film like an MCU film as her background is making indie (sort of) films.

I was sure that her core strengths lie in putting the focus on the characters rather than the plot. this is of course an assumption that I have since I haven't seen her earlier works like ‘Nomadland’ and ‘Songs My Brother Taught Me’(I'm guessing this is the title, lol) but the trailer and the vibe of those films always did give a more human vibe to it.

also, she's Asian and it's a very Asian thing to do to have a more character-driven story. this is also one of the reasons I love Korean movies and drama. so of course I was positively optimistic despite the reception.

Coming back to Eternals, I think I can say that this was one of the better MCU films I've seen. and I'm a big MCU head. haven't missed an MCU film except for black widow (which I don't plan on watching anyway)

the only possible Con I could think of was that maybe it's a Lil slow for some people's taste. but I would argue that being slow and putting more focus on the characters is what made it so good. The stakes were grand, cosmic actually. And you get a feeling of existentialism because of that.

the burden of responsibility and the choice to be made was shown well.

choosing between planetary destruction and entire universes not getting a chance to exist; what would you choose? I guess you can also relate it to abortion or using a condom. is it really wrong that something never existed in the first place?

apart from that, every character had their own philosophy and purpose for being. their own sadness their own guilt. it was beautiful truly. I think it would be fair to say this was a movie without any villains.

Was Arishem a villain? deffo not. he's pretty much god in this context and his purpose is beyond mere human comprehension. is he right in his purpose? maybe, maybe not. which is why it is interesting.

Were the deviants evil? not really. they were just programmed to kill. that one deviant that got sentient. I don't think I can really hate him even. all this time he just watched his brethren be slaughtered. so even though not he's sentient and can understand the purpose of the celestial.

So was Ikaris the bad guy? No he was just doing what he was designed to do for the greater good. also, he wasn't too thrilled about killing billions of earthlings either.

Kingo's love for movies came from the bond he shared with Sprite and he missed her and the time when she would do those visual things in those historic times.

Sprite just wanted to live, but couldn't without being a jailbait. Tinkerbell's story indeed as Kingo rightly said.

Makkari was cool and her dynamic with Druig was interesting and nice to see. fun fact she is played by an actual deaf person. that's extra cool

Druig might hint a bit of a god complex at times. but he just wanted to save people. for him, it was always people first.

Phastos was under the weight of being the reason behind humanity's advancements which by itself caused wars and deaths. him finding a reason to stop giving up hope on humanity was his family and also the reason he went back to the fight.

I liked Sersi and Dane Whitman together. they are nice even tho he knows nothing(get it)

Thena and Gilgamesh, ugh my heart aches. they were beautiful. RIP Gilg. you ruled and you did something every man should learn to do; you never gave up on Thena and were with her till the end and protected her till the end. if anyone's a chad, it's you, ma man\!

Also Thena, the god of war. weight of your memories. this is so real. *what is a man but his memories..* and you showed the importance of them. you rock too.

Overall a solid film. maybe some MCU fans aren't used to this. well, suck to be you.

highly recommended. go watch. now\!

# Jojo watch order

ok. jojo.

why do people need to start at part 1?

do they really?

lets see part 1 is the shortest but at the same time has the highest drop rate. has no meme ref people have seen around.

over all not a good part to start off of.

...

instead start with part 2\. not to skip part 1 but just start with part 2\.

honestly part 1 can be optional but i think you can enjoy part 1 way more if you have seen some of jojo first.

so see part 2\. part 2 is anyway epic af.

part 1 then seems like a prequel then.

so i can think of 2 routes

**Route Hamon** : part 2→part 1→part 3→part 4→part 5→part 6

**Route Stand:** part 2→part 3→part 1→part 4→part 5→part 6

**Route hamon** is nice as you are already into jojo by the time you reach part 1 as joseph is awesome. i think he's still the best jojo till date (but only young part 2 joseph, not the old one)

then when you enter part 1 you see the legacy of jonathan the gentleman as the og jojo and also learn about dio.

learning about dio now is good as you get to see of him right away in part 3 which you will watch next. and you also get to see him in his prime.

**orr...**

You could take **Stand route** now the stand route also start with part 2 but we call it stand route as you can get into stand quicker.

here you again start with joseph. you can't go wrong with that.

and then enter part 3 with stands. and by this time you aren't attached to hamon anyway so there's no massive shift causing you them withdrawls. plus you enter the meme territory earlier and can enjoy jojo for what you expected.

you wont be knowing much about the backstory of dio as you didn't see part 1 but thats ok. cuz you dont need to really.

Think of how crouching tiger did it. it was actually the 4th book of a series that was made into the movie and even without context on the backstory it worked(and nabbbed oscars)

So just learn about dio directly in part 3 and then watch part 1 as a prequel and understand where it all started. seeing dio as a living God and then seeing him as a teenager slowly becoming evil makes much more sense and will be a much better route to take.

moving on part 4 after this will be a treat as well.. cuz part 4 is handsdown the best jojo part ever.

Route stand is better. easy.

# Day 26 Why i love harry potter and why i cant care about LOTR

First 2 parts being directed by chris columbus makes it perfect. as its a magical journey. the messaging is all about immersing the viewer in to this new magical world with harry. and we as viewer ARE harry at the same time. it has nostaligia and magic in the best possible way. and overall the movie is very hopeful and bravery themed. very much apt for gryffindor. at the same time its not complicated as its made for kids orignally

Part 3 directed by alphonse cuaron elevates the game by 10\. the darker yet still harry pottery aspect gives it nuance. also we see the world in a slightly newer light. its not dark and depressy but rather a lived in world and even though magic is there its not the same as the first 2 parts as harry is older and used to these things now and since we are harry. we are too.

Part 5 is darker than previous parts but its very naturalistic progression after cauron established the new tone in part 3\. also sirius’s death is beyond tragic. bellatrix couldn’t have been better cast. marla singer is GOAT.

when you reach part 6, The story and characters have much more nuance to them. also part 6 is my personal favourite. character dynamics are explored better. harry for once is a good student. he’s now a character with actual growth and its really gratifying to see. part 6 also had that really heartfelt ending. oof.

The final 2 parts are really beautiful. the epic conclusion to the saga. the war. the journey finding the horcruxes. it’s just effing great. its like an epic adventure story i wouldn’t have cared about usually but this is followed after 6 great films which has set the context, the story and charcaters for me. its personal now. its not battle for howarts anymore. its battle for my house. and people who lived in there with me.

its all or nothing.

i wanted to write about lotr as well. but i got a lil more swept on the harry potter route. couldnt really get into LOTR so much because how much outside of the relatability element: Lord of the Rings is . Essentially, when I watch Harry Potter, the fantasy element is something that elevates the movie, but when I watch Lord of the Rings, there is not a single shred of relatability. Perhaps there is more on the human emotions and camaraderie side of things, but the entire set and environment and background is so outside my world that even though I did watch it, it took me like six or seven attempts to finally watch it. Harry Potter has been a very loved series of movies. A lot of it is also because I watched it as a child, so I had a stronger anchor. These days, even things related to Harry Potter are not enough to pull me in, but any older Harry Potter films, if it plays, it's always a game time. It always takes me to the world. It always makes me remember Harry of those times. I think that's the beauty of Harry Potter: it makes you feel something. It touches upon the part of yours that was curious about magic, the part that wants to escape, and I think that's probably why we people like Lord of the Rings, but for a different reason. Lord of the Rings is complete escapism or complete security within themselves where they don't need to feel the relatable angle; they just want to be dazzled, and Lord of the Rings delivers.

Honestly, I really don't know what my opinion is on this and why my opinion is this way. By "I don't know," I mean I don't know what it says about me, why the relatable element makes this big of a difference. Clearly, Lord of the Rings is not a bad film; it's a generally celebrated film, and people love it dearly. It is a pretty deep movie series, so the exploration here is less about if Lord of the Rings is bad or good; it's more about why Harry Potter has stayed with me even though I'm going to be 30\. When I originally wrote the first few lines of this article about 5-6 years ago, it stayed with me then as well, but Lord of the Rings maybe I need to grow up and maybe that's the difference ..

……

# Notes on Live upto your name (kdrama)

1. Live up to your name was surprisingly a fun watch. the time travel element is both ways giving a better narrative than simply a man out of time(i’m looking at you rooftop prince)  
2. the doctor and the female lead travelling back and forth made the show much fresher than your average jump flick.  
3. The romance was seriously well done. the progression happened without any cliches and by the time the first clear indication happened it was very obvious that they were already pretty much a couple  
4. For clarification, the first clear indication was when the female lead is being treated for her wound she got from the sword. and the nurse asks if he is her boyfriend. where she firstly doesn't deny and the main guy replies he’s not...yet. that cheeky “yet” was a perfect set-up.  
5. Most of it is their conversation are regarding their own principles and understanding of what it means to be a doctor. giving a much more interesting look into them as people and the overall story Than just doing a “will they wont they” for 9 to 11 episodes.  
6. Not putting the focus on loveline in the first half of the show removes any fatigue in viewers as well as they keep waiting for that penultimate episode in the show they are watching. So by not teasing us with breadcrumbs like other shows do it ended up nailing the romance aspect very well.  
7. this is not to say there should be no love or affection in the first half of story rather the focus shouldn’t be that. even live up to your name had moments where Ho Im is shown to be missing the girl but its out of affection and this plays well into their dynamic then and also acts as a previously laid context.  
8. Basically you can keep elements of the leads actually liking each other. its not a crime but whats important is not going overbord. and more importantly focus towards the purpose and the story of the show. we can’t have blank slate lovebird with no personality. just ensure their personality is what defines them not the fact that they are lover people.

# Notes on Vincenzo

## **Proud Father? really?**

**There is a flashback scene where he's shown to be proud of her daughter as she's Tenacious.**

Hong cha Young's father. in **Episode 3 or 4\. And he's just not telling her that he's proud yet as he doesn't want her to know this yet.**

for Starters Hong cha Young's a bad person. and its not a cheeky small time crook sorta stuff either. She's been directly involved in causing Misery to innocent people. Bribing people to ensure justice only favours the rich and evil\*\*.\*\* she worked for a corporation and directly supported them in doing super illegal deeds all while knowing how its fucking up with the innocent people. she’s not shown to be remorseful to anything. **she’s simply indifferent. there is no moral code.**

**Her being a bad person is not a problem** but her dad even after having a strong moral code and going as far as disowning her (tried on paper at least) is shown to be proud of her.

This was the **first major lack of nuance**.

The set-up was already fine. **He's good** \- **she's evil**. He is disappointed in her but can't help but believe that there's still some goodness in her.

That's as simple as it needs to be. The proud scene makes everything obsolete. It should simply have been a belief. Cuz he's a father.

Cha Young's bad and she should’ve known that her dad died still disappointed in her.

This would've been a good reason for her to do what needs to be done to get her father justice and all.

## **Hong cha young’s leading a weird arc**

Her resolve for fighting babel (the evil company) is strictly cuz they got her father killed. the reason she is on the good side is purely because of that. there’s been no self reflection. which means that change of path is not much of arc at all. nothing keeps her up from lobbying and fighting cases for company that literally kill people. 5 episodes in and nothings changed yet either

## **Where are your balls Vincenzo?**

Vincenzo not killing any of the 2 guys in episode 4 was a **super pussy move**. He's already killed people before and that too without batting an eye in ep1.

The whole scaring with props and fake blood was the most disappointing thing. These were bad guys who kill and get people killed. And you are already a guy who is more than capable of delivering Revenge.

in the very least the first guy they fake shot could've been the real shot even if it didn't actually kill him off.

**Cha Young realising what monster Vincenzo is could've made it all much more interesting**. Her being scared was all an act and hence all that emotion she went through is wasted.

For what? 2 murderers?

Imagine her stomach seeing someone get shot but she is immobile cus of shock. Interesting opportunity but lost.

Also after this incident Vincenzo could've told her this is how he does things. She is supposed to quit if she interferes. And even after witnessing 2 people(or at least 1\) being shot. She still decides to stay. Cuz she wants justice for her dad, whatever the cost.

Great opportunity wasted. Because they have no Balls. If it's not a dark and serious crime drama we will have to encompass any testicles to be great

## **What’s with the Intern**

I really like that guy. and honestly her being paired with cha young made more sense than our lead. although its only been 5 episodes but still. they should ensure his feelings for cha young is genuine and he really wants to protect her despite being the villain.

Making him the villain seemed a bit weird as his motivation to join the lawyers company as an intern make no sense (till ep 5 at least, although what good excuse can you anyway give?) but its still interesting as there is potential in the story to make it something cool. However the trend in the show makes me think otherwise.

(the issue isn't that he’s a villain but his association with the lawyer company make less sense)

The intern has bit of bromance with our vincenzo and I quite enjoyed it. keeping him the villain and him still being genuine in these scene will make him a much more interesting villain than just a shock bail

## **That female prosecutor lady says “asshole”. (Ssyabalra) 쌰발라**

This was another unnuanced take. her saying the word asshole in a country accent seemed nice at first but its overused to a point it seems like a gimmick.

its like the writer went and asked her

“can you pull of an Asshole in a rustic country-ish accent”

which she could and she did. Super well that too. And so the writer got a massive erection and filled the entire script with 쌰발라. is it supposed to be ssibal in a country accent? idfk.

Anyway that’s the only thing I can think of, that the writer became a bit of a try-hard since he saw a good actor in place.

## **Other weird decisions:**

Vincenzo learns that the chairman of babel is fake by asking a trivia question about super specific authors’ quotes. really? that's his reasoning to find that? you could’ve even gone with the generic “gut feeling” bullshit and that would've been a better reason.

They save the building demolitions with a party. Wth man? really? that's just lame. cant you come up with something clever or convincing? this is just lazy writing.

## **Mainly it’s the writing**

If I had to pin **all the issues** in this show it's the writing. they are fine in some places but seriously disappointing in others.

## **Overall verdict so far**

1. Plot is good. solid  
2. Production and cinematography is pretty damn good.  
3. The style is pretty much on point. Be in the wardrobe or mannerisms. Cha-young and Vincenzo specially.  
4. Cha Young and Vincenzo have a really fun dynamic but there's not much of a romantic chemistry. Which is not to say it's a bad thing. In fact could be preferable even.  
5. Great cast and their performance is pretty good too. they are all really darn good.  
6. **Writing and execution are where they are a bit too uneven**. it's trying to be dark but holding punches on moments it could define itself as a category leader

Side note:

I really like cha Young's though. Mainly I'm biased cuz of Be Melo. But also cuz that she's goofy and strong and brash. Not to mention she’s directionless and really well dressed which make her even more likeable despite the fact her character is anything but.

# Notes on Light in your eyes (kdrama)

## **Bad Characters**

Bad characters are good for character arcs but you need to plant seeds to show there is some world where they are not insufferable. Also the difference between bad people and annoying characters. you can redeem genocide fueling folks with good narrative (Magath from Attack on titan) but rarely possible to redeem annoying or insufferable characters. The whole “She is misunderstood character” doesn't work if she is a prick.

### **Not so well Written characters**

* **Old Hyeja** She is kinda annoying. this is coming from me who likes how old characters are handled in a show. ironically I love the younger Hyeja more. her brattiness and sorrow felt genuine as a 25-year-old girl but the older one is kinda a brat. and not even in a sweet way. also, every time she tells Nam Joo hyuk things like “don't you miss hyena” I get annoyed. Lady\! He just met her 2-3 times. why are you being so weird? Even our chad Lead says that they weren’t anything more than strangers she persists on them being a thing. It was like how in high school would tease each other and say “you have a crush on Candice right?\!\! don't deny it\! I know it”. Ah so annoying. (*can deez nu-)*

   Shes’ also pretty dumb and doesn’t know how to use the watch. every attempt is her failing 500 times before succeeding. even for suspension of disbelief, that's a bit much.

* **(OIL \- Old Insufferable Lady)** the first grumpy lady she befriends is insufferable. she went through her arc now but her piss poor character wasn’t redeemed. I cant empathise with her pain. but in that too the Old insufferable lady has a scene where she gives the lead her pills and suggests he kill himself. it’s official. she is the OG league of legend player. Even in one of those episodes where she isn’t annoying (Episode 9, which is a good episode tbh) Me: damn my boss is so annoying OIL: Why don't you kill your self

Jim: my head hurts a bit. it's kinda annoying OIL: Have you considered death?

Pam: too much fine dust in the air no OIL: *you know the rules and so do I...*

* **The Older brother(Young-su)** is really pathetic. It's been 8 episodes and they still haven't shown an angle or a redeeming quality yet. I don't hate him it's just that he’s a failed excuse for a human being. plus the Barbecue incident could have easily been used as a reveal that he actually was trying to kill himself. would have not made the character into a total joke. Edit: Episode 10\. They are making it worse with the whole Pee in the bottle thing. Edit 2\. he drank the pee. perfect. just when you thought things could be worse. they deployed an interesting way of showing the fact that he drank it which is funny since the one time the show chooses to use show don't tell and is subtle is the time it uses on somethings as vile as a pathetic character drinking his own piss. Honestly, I feel bad for the girl who likes him.  
* **The old guy who has a crush on Hyeja (He isn’t the problem but how Hyeja interacts with him)** He might be a bit creepy but old Hyeja being the annoying gal she is really is blue balling the poor dude. calling him ugly despite him being nice to her. the character is been left to be nothing more than comic relief. despite him being loyal to fault character. Edit: Episode 10\. ok, maybe they are planning to make him look cool now. better late than never but it could also mean he might die by the end to get a hero ending.  
* **The insurance duo:** I liked them earlier but they become pricks by the end of episode 9, character like these are kept slimy to subvert expectation and show that they have some sense of moral compass and would go the evil route. They did the reverse here. slimy characters are generally not liked much anyway. but kept hope that this is a good opportunity for some nice heartfelt scenes in the future. but alas they tuned out to be worse assholes than you would expect them to be. ah well Edit: Episode 10\. they are worse now. even killing someone is fair game now. wut? ok.

## **The Good Things**

* The Premise and the main idea: the Premise itself is pretty amazing.  
* Hyeja’s Friends: I like both of them. especially the Chinese restaurant girl.  
* Episode 10’s first 1 minute 50 seconds.  
* The Dream episode: Really really well executed. even though I was like I hope this isn't a dream episode as it would be a cop-out. But I was pleasantly surprised by the execution and the narrative route they took to nail its ending

### **Episode 9**

* This is where it starts getting good. the scene where the old folks come out with signs outside the police station is pretty heartfelt. and handled quite well.  
* Episode 9 feels nice. it's sad but in a good way so far.  
* Nam Joohyuk has been solo carrying this show and he’s shining in this episode. he’s really a good actor and is doing a fan-fucking-tastic job in every shot he is in this episode.  
* Also by the end of episode 9, I don’t hate the OIL and it is a bit sad to see her go. not that it discounts her previous OIL-ness(wut) but at least the show felt sincere and the moments intended by the show are landing well  
* Another good point, the brother is finally started turning around. despite being a failed human, I always wanted him to turn his life around or better start making good choices. I’m a bit scared his relationship might not work out as the show is finally gearing to make the remaining episodes a sob story. fingers crossed that doesn't happen and this couple makes it through. I'm biased since I have seen him in some other show and hence root for him regardless of how much of a waste of space he is.

Also, the point that I’m making about episode 9 being the good one doesn’t mean the previous episodes were shit. they were good too but it's just that they couldn’t hide their inner workings and wanted to capitalise on the heartfelt moments but they just couldn't carry out the deed of writing characters to feel as sincere as they could have been.

### **Final thoughts**

Light in your eyes has all the right elements. The cinematography is fine and low key. The actors are fantastic. Namjoo Hyuk is great

But overall: The wires are visible. they are trying to pick the best practices of all the show which deals with the reality of life and how tough it is, and trying to stretch it to the max. which is why they are failing at it. nuance is what you need in the characters you write.

But still, **a solid 7.5 out of 10 (that feels 7 at times cuz of the issues)**

## **Notes on the last 3 episodes and The sudden shift.**

**Edit: I Ended Episode 10**. Oh boy, the only way I can describe is a car that made all the wrong turns but somehow parallelly parked at the end.

the Whole section from the moment the old guy tries giving the watch to Hyeja at the end and we see some memory fragments watch amazing. generally, it's a cop-out move. But just like the earlier dream episode, they landed it well. One thing I would do differently would be that she doesn't mention she had Alzheimer's at the end (in this episode). that way a cosy mystery is maintained.

### **The Final 2 episodes (and the last 9 minutes of ep 10\)**

This is where the show suddenly becomes really really fucking good.

it's almost like the real show writer was on a vacation and so the interns were writing in the beginning. And then he returned and saw the absolute state of the show. So he decided to fix the show by literally doing a total overhaul.

Even though it’s a bit of a joke but I sorta genuinely believe this lol. cuz that how big the shift was in these 2 episodes.

Young Hyeja was great as usual and so were her friends. the moments where the old Hyeja is shown are all really well done. she is no more annoying in these episodes and actually a character you root for. it's not a perspective shift though. cuz I can still go back to the earlier episodes and I’ll still find her annoying, it's only because of the better writing and story in the last 2 episodes that she becomes a good character.

the sorrowful moments are impactful and don't seem try-hard even once. The post-Joon ho death Hyeja is stoic and stellar, It’s harrowing to see her not break down on the news of her dead husband. her indifference to her son is painful but in a good way. shes surely wasn’t a good mom but she didn’t hate her child. some folks might assume the fact that she used to swipe the snowy stairs make her a good mom but that would be an incorrect reading. She was a bad mom but still cared as she is a mother at the end of the day and the fact that she wasn't a great mom is the regret she has when she is old. which is why she tries to be extra nice to her and thinks of him very fondly after getting old and forgetting a major chunk of her memories. It’s regret.

Everything in the last 2 episodes has impactful moments, be it the contrast in character traits

## **Verdict**

This doesn't make my hall of fame purely because of the 1st 8 episodes cus the last 4 episodes are definitely hall of fame material. overall 8.5/10 (could've been a 9.5 if not the first )

IMO Episodes 1-8 should have been compressed to 3 episodes. and episode number 10 also be shortened. and 11,12 remain as is.

making this a 6-7 episode story with a tight narrative

…….

# Notes on Multiverse of Madness

TLDR: I liked the first part better. Reasons?

## **The first Doctor Strange film**

I watched the First Doctor Strange movie in 2016 and it was an experience like no other. suffice to say the movie slapped my ass cheeks harder than my parents ever did.

It was brilliant.

Every cameo or extended appearance of doctor strange since then has been nothing short of magical. Be it his brief appearance in Thor Ragnarok or his beautiful Multi-arm display in Infinity war not to forget his appearance in No way home.

## **Then What Happened here?**

The end credits rolled and I discovered the director’s name and all the pieces suddenly made sense. Sam Raimi, The same guy who made the original spiderman trilogy and the Evil dead movies. But most importantly the TV series *Ash and the Evil Dead*.

Multiverse of Madness had full of mind-boggling sequences and the production was top notch. But despite that, the film never felt magical. It felt like the Evil Dead edition of a Marvel film. in fact it was the least Marvel-ly I have ever felt in a Marvel film.

### **It Gets Dark and Violent**

Holy shit, the other doctor strange caused an entire universe to be destroyed. Trillions and gazillions of people died because of our hero. what are the stakes come to? It took **a decade to save about half** of the universe. And suddenly we hear an entire reality’s end caused by 1 man like it's nothing more than a plot point to say “this one is a grief-ridden boi, very sad right”

### **The Scarlet Witch and the Terrible writing to justify the premise**

“I am a mother so I'm being nice and not killing people.”

Else?

“well, I will kill people. a lot of them. even important ones. like other superheroes”

### **The on the nose references**

Let's make Doctor strange do that cool hand thingy he did in the infinity war. people went wild over that. And to make sure they get it make him do it multiple times. what do you mean it will be really apparent that we are milking by doing it 3 times in the span of 1 movie. Nonsense, i think you haven’t heard of references.

Also, the female captain America has to say *“I can do this all day.”* and if possible kill her within 60 seconds of her trying to be a wannabe badass.

### **The terrible fan service**

Prof X in the film was nothing more than fanservice and a really cheap one. I could help but eye-roll when he waltzed in on a giant yellow dildo. the man already died with his honour intact in Logan(sorta). why are we still beating the dead horse, figuratively I mean.

who are you pandering to with this? an X-men fan? do those still exist?

### **Terrible writing in Resolution 1**

Hey kid, you can do it.

Oh, really it didn't occur to me thanks. now I can do

### **Terrible writing in Resolution 2**

I’m Scarlett witch, I'm a mass-murdering psychopatch, I’ll become a good person in a coin flip. thanks, doc. you’re the smartest

### **No Likeable character.**

Everyone is an insufferable douchebag. every character in the other universe is an asshole. funnily the only character who isn’t is Wanda from that universe. what an irony

Fuck the council. Illuminati? really? glad they fucking died except I couldn’t enjoy their deaths as it was so fucked up.

## **Its not a bad film though. (i still fucking hate it)**

The production is Stellar, and the premise is solid albeit the way they decided to present it was terrible.

On the other side. many folks liked the darker element of the film as they are already past the marvel fatigue. So in case you also did pass that stage already then yes you might like this one more than I did.

Oh btw I liked America, she was sweet. but why is her name America and why is no one finding it strange? I guess Strange is strange but America Chavez is a perfectly fine name?

or is it supposed to be a Mexican name (Chavez) \+ America= hence it’s clever?

……

# Why the Handmaiden is not a lesbian film

* The character in the movie love each other and are girls. yes. But the handmaiden doesn’t delve into the subject of same-sex love or things like taboo or a self-discovery.  
* Maybe they were bisexuals. maybe they weren’t even lesbians. they were simply *each-other-sexual*. which would basically mean they were straight but they only fell in love with each other. This is not to deny that they were lesbians but rather the film isn’t. And is beyond all that.  
* It’s a film independent of all that. it’s simply about love and not lesbian love.  
* There is not a single line of dialogue on being a lesbian especially since it was actually set in a time when it was a major taboo.  
* Films, like ‘Call me by your name’ and, ‘Blue is the warmest colour’ explore the LGBTQ dynamics in the movie and are evident from the narrative.  
* This is what makes the handmaiden different from the rest.  
* The handmaiden is a great film. one of my all-time favourites and is possibly the second coming of Christ.

# Why Shinji is a pussy, and everyone hates him.

written in 2022; before my rerun of evangellion in 2025; when it finally became one of my favorite anime.

## **The original comment from someone on youtube comments:**

It's funny that they compare Bojack and Shinji. Because I've seen more people who feel sorry and even love Bojack, a 50-year-old mentally abusive alcoholic narcissist, and absolutely despise Shinji, a 14-year boy who's been neglected, emotionally detached and frightened when out in life-threatening situations. Yes, Shinji was whiny, but I really never understood the hate he got. As if you wouldn't be scared fucking shitless if you were in his position.

## **My thoughts/ response to that:**

It's the same reason people love Walter White or Jaime at the end of season 3 of GOT. But they hate that fish-killing girl from finding Nemo. (A drug lord, an incestuous murderer on one hand… And an 8-year-old girl with bad dentures on the other)

### **Why?**

A character's actions aren't as impactful as the narrative that portrays them. Shinji is placed as a wimp by the writer. You can pity him but not relate with him too much.

Whereas with Bojack you don't pity him. But the narrative makes you feel like you've felt the way Bojack feels. Even though you've not done the horrible things he's done.

### **It also has to do with the setting:**

* Bojack has to deal with the trauma of day-to-day life, it's a regular setting.  
* While Shinji has to fight Hot Milfs and Galactic Kaijus while sitting in a cannibalistic mech.
